description: Galbi Korean BBQ Short Ribs are a beloved classic featuring tender, marinated beef short ribs grilled to caramelized perfection. This iconic dish offers a harmonious blend of sweet, savory, and umami flavors, making it a cornerstone of Korean cuisine. Enjoy these succulent ribs with rice and an array of banchan for an unforgettable meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Rinse the flanken cut beef short ribs under cold water to remove any bone fragments. Pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels. If desired, trim any excess fat.

instructions.title: Blend the Marinade Ingredients
instructions.text: In a blender or food processor, combine the soy sauce, water, brown sugar, mirin, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, grated Asian pear, and grated onion. Blend until the mixture is smooth and well combined. Add black pepper.

instructions.title: Marinate the Ribs
instructions.text: Place the prepared short ribs in a large shallow dish or a resealable plastic bag. Pour the marinade over the ribs, ensuring all pieces are fully coated. Cover the dish or seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight for best flavor.

instructions.title: Preheat Grill or Broiler
instructions.text: When ready to cook, preheat your outdoor grill to medium-high heat (about 400F / 200C). If using a broiler, preheat it to high and line a baking sheet with foil.

instructions.title: Cook the Galbi
instructions.text: Remove the ribs from the marinade, letting any excess drip off. Place the ribs on the preheated grill. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, flipping once, until nicely caramelized and cooked to your desired doneness. For broiler, cook 4-6 minutes per side, watching carefully to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Galbi to a serving platter. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions. Serve immediately with steamed rice and various Korean side dishes like kimchi and ssamjang.

tips: For truly tender Galbi, consider scoring the meat against the grain a few times before marinating, or ask your butcher for a 'butterfly cut' to ensure even cooking and maximum flavor absorption.
If you cannot find Asian pear, a ripe Bosc pear or even a Fuji apple can be used as a substitute. Alternatively, 1/4 cup of apple juice can provide a similar tenderizing effect and sweetness.

Galbi is best enjoyed fresh off the grill. To prevent overcooking and drying out the meat, always monitor closely and cook until just tender with beautiful caramelization. Serve immediately with rice and fresh lettuce wraps.
